source_evidence.observation: The proposition takes independent, mean-zero, sub-gaussian random variables X_1, ..., X_N and states both that their sum from i = 1 to N is sub-gaussian and that its squared psi_2 norm is at most an absolute constant C times the sum of the squared psi_2 norms of the summands.

The squared psi_2 norm satisfies ||sum_{i=1}^N X_i||_{psi_2}^2 <= C sum_{i=1}^N ||X_i||_{psi_2}^2, where C is an absolute constant (PDF page 17, printed page 28, displayed inequality and following sentence of Proposition 2.6.1).
definitions_and_conventions: The notation ||.||_{psi_2} denotes the book's psi_2 norm for sub-gaussian random variables; its defining normalization is inherited from the preceding section and is not restated in the selected proposition (PDF page 17, printed page 28, displayed norm inequality; PDF page 18, printed page 29, reference to Definition 2.5.6).

The summation is the unweighted finite sum with index i running from 1 through N; no coefficients, identical-distribution assumption, or common psi_2 bound are part of Proposition 2.6.1 (PDF page 17, printed page 28, proposition statement and display).

'Mean zero' applies componentwise, E X_i = 0 for every i, in the standard random-variable convention used by the statement (PDF page 17, printed page 28, phrase 'X_1, ..., X_N be independent, mean zero, sub-gaussian random variables').

'Independent' applies to the displayed finite family, not merely to the sum or to an unspecified pair (PDF page 17, printed page 28, same opening phrase; PDF page 18, printed page 29, product factorization marked 'by independence').
The exponent 2 on the left applies to the psi_2 norm of the entire sum, and every summand's psi_2 norm is also squared on the right (PDF page 17, printed page 28, displayed inequality).

An 'absolute constant' is a universal numerical constant independent of N and of the particular random variables and their laws; no numerical value is asserted (PDF page 17, printed page 28, closing clause; PDF page 18, printed page 29, constants C and C_1 in the proof).

The source is working with real-valued random variables: the proof evaluates E exp(lambda times the sum) for every lambda in R (PDF page 18, printed page 29, first proof display).

Sub-gaussianity and the psi_2 norm carry the book's inherited definitions and equivalent MGF characterization, specifically the proof's references to property (2.16), Proposition 2.5.2, and Definition 2.5.6 (PDF page 18, printed page 29).

The family and sum are finite. The conventional reading is a positive finite index N, but the statement does not explicitly state N >= 1 or define an empty-family case (PDF page 17, printed page 28, notation X_1, ..., X_N and sum from 1 to N).

No identical-distribution hypothesis appears (PDF page 17, printed page 28, Proposition 2.6.1).

The estimate has one absolute multiplicative constant C outside the right-hand finite sum (PDF page 17, printed page 28, display and closing clause).
C is independent of N and all X_i; the proof may pass through other absolute constants and absorb them into the proposition's C (PDF page 18, printed page 29, definitions of K^2 and C_1).

undebatable_constraints: All three assumptions apply to the full family: independence, mean zero for each X_i, and sub-gaussianity for each X_i (PDF page 17, printed page 28, opening sentence of Proposition 2.6.1).
The result concerns the unweighted finite sum sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 17, printed page 28, both conclusions of Proposition 2.6.1).
Both conclusions are required: the sum is sub-gaussian, and its squared psi_2 norm obeys the displayed estimate (PDF page 17, printed page 28, sentence and display of Proposition 2.6.1).

The quantitative conclusion is squared-norm subadditivity up to a universal factor: ||sum_i X_i||_{psi_2}^2 <= C sum_i ||X_i||_{psi_2}^2; neither the squares nor the inequality direction may be dropped or reversed (PDF page 17, printed page 28, displayed inequality).

C is absolute: it cannot depend on N, on i, or on the particular variables or their distributions, although its numerical value is not specified (PDF page 17, printed page 28, closing clause; PDF page 18, printed page 29, proof constants).

The proposition does not require the X_i to be identically distributed and does not replace their individual psi_2 norms by a maximum (PDF page 17, printed page 28, statement and displayed right-hand side).

The source's inherited real-valued sub-gaussian and psi_2 conventions must be used; changing scalar domain or norm normalization is not licensed by the selected passage (PDF page 18, printed page 29, real-lambda MGF and references to the book's Definition 2.5.6).

contract_plain_english: In the real-valued sub-gaussian setting inherited from the book, take a finite family X_1, ..., X_N of independent random variables, each centered and sub-gaussian. Their unweighted sum is again sub-gaussian, and there is a universal numerical constant C, independent of N and of all the variables, such that the square of the sum's psi_2 norm is at most C times the sum of the squares of the individual psi_2 norms. The proposition does not explicitly state N >= 1, an empty-sum convention, the underlying probability space, the psi_2 normalization, or a numerical value of C (PDF page 17, printed page 28, Proposition 2.6.1; clarified by the proof continuation on PDF page 18, printed page 29).
